findings.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53 — A single try/catch wraps the whole sequential cancel loop, so one SendGrid error (bad/duplicate batch, rate limit, timeout) aborts cancellation of every later cancelled reminder in that run (their emails still go out to cancelled bookings) and also skips the deferred lazy PrismaPromise deletes of rows it already cancelled, so the same poison row blocks every run until its scheduledDate passes.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:225 — Soft-cancel only sets a DB flag and leaves the SendGrid send live until the cron cancels it in the last hour before scheduledDate, so a booking cancelled less than one cron interval (or SendGrid's cancel lead time) before the reminder, or on any deployment where the cron isn't running, still gets the reminder email. Before this change it was cancelled in SendGrid right away.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — The immediateDelete path cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or flags the DB row. If a booking was soft-cancelled by requestReschedule and the attendee then reschedules through handleNewBooking (which accepts CANCELLED originals), the row keeps cancelled=true and the cron re-POSTs a cancel for an already-cancelled batch, which can throw and trigger the loop abort above.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:488 — Reminder cancellation is now fire-and-forget: the DB update/delete is not awaited or included in Promise.all and errors are swallowed by console.log. The old code awaited the deletes, so a DB failure or serverless teardown after the response now silently leaves the reminder active (same pattern in bookings.tsx requestReschedule and workflows.tsx update).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — The try/catch around forEach with un-awaited async delete calls can never catch anything, so the "Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders" log is dead code and failures pass silently.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — A single failed SendGrid cancel throws out of the whole loop, so later cancelled reminders never get cancelled and the deletes queued for earlier ones (lazy Prisma promises, never awaited) never run; the same batches get re-POSTed on every cron run until they age out.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — The immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or flags the DB row, so on reschedule in handleNewBooking (no cascade) the row lingers as a live scheduled reminder and a failed cancel is swallowed with no retry.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:48 — Soft-cancelled reminders are only cancelled on a later cron run, so a reminder due before the next run (or under SendGrid's 10-minute cutoff) is still sent for a cancelled booking, and the past-due deleteMany then purges it with no cancel ever sent.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:180 — If twilio.cancelSMS throws (for example, the SMS was already sent or cancelled), the workflowReminder row delete is skipped, leaving stale rows that the old code always deleted.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:968 — After requestReschedule has already soft-cancelled a booking's reminders, rebooking through handleNewBooking cancels the same batches immediately but leaves cancelled:true, so the cron POSTs a second cancel for an already-cancelled batch (which can hit the abort-on-error path).

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole loop and the lazily-built PrismaPromise deletes are never executed, so already-cancelled rows stay `cancelled: true` and get re-cancelled next run while later reminders go uncancelled

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid batch but neither deletes nor flags the WorkflowReminder row (reschedule path in handleNewBooking.ts:968), leaving a `scheduled: true, cancelled: null` row that looks live to every reader

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966 — Original booking reminders already flagged `cancelled: true` by requestReschedule get cancelled again right away here, and the cron later POSTs cancel a second time for the same batch_id; SendGrid can reject that and stall the cancel loop

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:230 — Cancellation is now only a DB flag that the cron picks up later, so a reminder due before the next cron tick is still sent for a cancelled/rescheduled booking (the old code cancelled in SendGrid right away)

packages/prisma/migrations/20230217230604_add_cancelled_to_workflow_reminder/migration.sql:2 — No rollback plan: if app code is rolled back, rows already flagged `cancelled: true` are ignored by the old code and their SendGrid batches are never cancelled

packages/prisma/migrations/20230217230604_add_cancelled_to_workflow_reminder/migration.sql:2 — Migration file existed empty in the base commit and was edited in place; any env that already recorded it as applied (empty) will never get the column, and every workflowReminder query fails with a missing-column error

packages/prisma/schema.prisma:644 — cancelled Boolean?` has no default, so existing rows are NULL (three states: null/false/true) and any future `cancelled: false` filter would silently miss them; use `Boolean @default(false)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:213 — The same EMAIL/SMS if/else dispatch to deleteScheduled*Reminder is copy-pasted across 7 call sites (workflows.tsx 213/377/520/575, bookings.tsx:489, handleCancelBooking.ts:487, handleNewBooking.ts:967) instead of one shared cancelWorkflowReminder(reminder) helper.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:200 — The `immediateDelete` boolean flag has a misleading name: it only cancels the batch in SendGrid and returns without deleting or flagging the DB row, and the default path of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` doesn't delete anything either, so the helper and flag names both misstate what they do.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:968 — The reschedule path passes immediateDelete=true, but the equivalent reschedule flow in bookings.tsx:490 soft-cancels, so the same lifecycle event uses the flag inconsistently and the old booking's reminder row here is never marked cancelled or deleted.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177 — deleteScheduledSMSReminder hard-deletes the DB row while the sibling deleteScheduledEmailReminder soft-cancels by default, so the paired helpers have different persistence semantics and callers have to know which one does what.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:54 — The cron types its promise array with Prisma's generated internal type `Prisma.Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient<WorkflowReminder, never>`, which is brittle across Prisma upgrades; it could just use Promise<unknown>[] or a single deleteMany.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — The SendGrid scheduled_sends cancel request is duplicated inline here and in emailReminderManager.ts:214 rather than living in one exported helper.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:10 — This new value import from "@calcom/prisma/client" (the types Prisma and WorkflowReminder) mixes Prisma import sources with the "@prisma/client" import on line 2 of the same file.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:2 — The type-only imports App, Credential, EventTypeCustomInput and Prisma were changed from `import type` to a value import, which blurs the type-only boundary this file had kept.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:9 — Prisma` is now imported as a value but no longer used anywhere in the file (dead import); it also lacks a trailing comma, so the import block doesn't match prettier style.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:2 — The type-only `PrismaPromise` was moved from `import type` into a runtime value import.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:901 — Unrelated churn strips all indentation from the commented-out sendTestReminder block, and the `// BookingInfo` import comment it depends on was removed, which makes the dead block harder to read or restore.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — The try/catch wraps a forEach of un-awaited async helpers that already swallow their own errors, so the catch/log.error branch can never run (dead error handling).
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:574 — The `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...)` callback keeps its `async` keyword but no longer awaits anything after the deleteMany was removed.
packages/prisma/schema.prisma:644 — The new `cancelled Boolean?` is nullable with no default, which creates a null/false/true tri-state where a non-null `Boolean @default(false)` would do.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — Cron awaits one SendGrid cancel HTTP call per cancelled reminder sequentially with no batch cap, so runtime grows linearly and, stacked before the existing sequential scheduling loop, risks the serverless function timeout

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:74 — Row deletes are lazy PrismaPromises run only after the whole loop, so a single SendGrid error or a timeout skips every delete and the same cancel calls are re-issued on every cron run until scheduledDate passes

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — New findMany on cancelled reminders has no take/limit or select and WorkflowReminder has no index on (cancelled, scheduledDate), adding another full-table scan and unbounded materialization each cron run

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:376 — Reminders for every booking of disabled event types are cancelled via one un-awaited single-row update/delete per reminder (unbounded concurrent queries) instead of a single batched updateMany/deleteMany

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — Cron cancel loop has one try/catch around every reminder, so the first SendGrid 400 (SendGrid returns this for an already-cancelled batch or a cancel within 10 min of send_at) aborts the loop; later cancelled reminders are skipped, and the lazy Prisma deletes at line 74 never run for batches that were already cancelled, so the next run re-POSTs them, gets 400 again and blocks the queue until the send times pass, and reminders for cancelled bookings still go out

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:225 — Soft-cancel moves the SendGrid cancel to the next cron run, but SendGrid rejects a cancel less than 10 min before send_at, so a booking cancelled or rescheduled shortly before a reminder's send time (about cron interval + 10 min) still gets the reminder, where the old code cancelled it immediately

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:488 — The cancelled=true DB write is now the only record that the SendGrid send must be cancelled, but it is fired inside forEach without await (the awaited Promise.all of reminder deletes was removed), so if serverless execution freezes after the response or the write fails (error is only console.logged), the reminder is never flagged and the email is sent

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:490 — requestReschedule fires reminder cancellation helpers without await (the previous await Promise.all(remindersToDelete) was removed), so the soft-cancel write can be lost or its failure swallowed, leaving the old booking's email and SMS reminders active

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — The immediateDelete path POSTs a SendGrid cancel but does not delete the row or set cancelled, so on reschedule (handleNewBooking) the row stays scheduled; a failed cancel (swallowed by console.log) has no retry, and if a workflow edit or event-type removal later soft-cancels the row, the cron sends a duplicate cancel that gets 400 and hits the P1 loop abort

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:214 — Workflow and step deletion (lines 214 and 521) fire immediateDelete SendGrid cancels without await and then cascade-delete the reminder rows (lines 220 and 527), so any failed cancel (e.g. SendGrid's per-account limit on active cancellations, or a cancel too close to send_at) is only console.logged, no row is left to retry, and the email is still sent

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — The try/catch around forEach with un-awaited async helpers cannot catch their failures (the promises reject asynchronously and the helpers already swallow errors), so the log.error branch is dead and reschedule-time cancellation failures are invisible

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:180 — The DB delete now runs after twilio.cancelSMS in the same try block, so a Twilio error (e.g. message already sent or not cancelable) skips the row delete and leaks the WorkflowReminder row; the old code deleted rows independently of the Twilio call

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:523 — Un-awaited SMS and null-referenceId email helpers race the awaited workflowStep.delete cascade at line 527, so their prisma.workflowReminder.delete throws P2025 on already-cascaded rows, producing spurious error logs that hide real cancellation failures

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — A single failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole loop and skips the lazy deletes, so the same row can fail again on every run and block all later soft-cancelled reminders, which then still email attendees about cancelled or rescheduled bookings (details and meeting URL)

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — Untested cron cancel loop: a single SendGrid failure (e.g. batch already cancelled via the immediateDelete path) aborts the whole loop and the lazily-built prisma deletes never execute, so the same reminder blocks all later cancellations on every run

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:203 — No tests cover the three new deleteScheduledEmailReminder branches (null referenceId hard-delete, immediateDelete SendGrid-only, soft-cancel update) even though every caller dropped the old `scheduled && referenceId` guard

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — immediateDelete branch cancels at SendGrid but neither deletes nor flags the DB row, leaving stale scheduled rows (e.g. after handleNewBooking reschedule) that can later be soft-cancelled and re-cancelled by cron; no test pins the expected row state

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — Soft-cancelled reminders are only cancelled at SendGrid when cron sees them within 1 hour of scheduledDate; no test covers the timing window (cancel shortly before send, cron cadence gaps) so emails for cancelled bookings may still go out

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966 — New reschedule reminder-cancel path is untested, including original bookings already CANCELLED by requestReschedule (soft-cancelled rows re-cancelled immediately) and a try/catch that cannot catch the un-awaited async helper failures

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:485 — Reminder cancellation became fire-and-forget (removed from the awaited Promise.all) and no test asserts reminders are soft-cancelled/deleted once the cancel handler resolves

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:488 — requestReschedule reminder cancellation switched to un-awaited soft-cancel/SMS-delete with no test verifying old-booking reminders end up cancelled

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:179 — deleteScheduledSMSReminder now owns row deletion but skips it when twilio.cancelSMS throws; no test covers null referenceId, Twilio failure, or already-deleted row

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:519 — Step-deleted (and workflow-delete at line 212) paths race un-awaited reminder deletes against cascade deletes from workflowStep.delete/workflow.deleteMany; no router test covers these paths

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:376 — activeOn-removal and step-edit (line 574) paths changed from hard delete to soft-cancel for email reminders with no test asserting cancelled-flag vs deletion per reminder state

This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53 — A single try/catch wraps the whole sequential cancel loop, so one SendGrid error (bad/duplicate batch, rate limit, timeout) aborts cancellation of every later cancelled reminder in that run (their emails still go out to cancelled bookings) and also skips the deferred lazy PrismaPromise deletes of rows it already cancelled, so the same poison row blocks every run until its scheduledDate passes.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` the new cancellation block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop and the final `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` in a single `try/catch`. Any thrown error from `await client.request(...)` for one reminder will jump to the `catch`, aborting cancellation for all subsequent reminders in `remindersToCancel`. Because Prisma deletes are only queued (pushed) and not awaited until after the loop, the catch also skips deleting rows for reminders already cancelled earlier in the loop, allowing a failing/“poison” reminder row to be retried and fail on every run while it matches the query window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:225 — Soft-cancel only sets a DB flag and leaves the SendGrid send live until the cron cancels it in the last hour before scheduledDate, so a booking cancelled less than one cron interval (or SendGrid's cancel lead time) before the reminder, or on any deployment where the cron isn't running, still gets the reminder email. Before this change it was cancelled in SendGrid right away.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` from immediately cancelling the SendGrid scheduled send to (by default) only doing `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true } })` and not calling SendGrid (`emailReminderManager.ts` now only calls SendGrid when `immediateDelete` is true). Most call sites in the diff (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `viewer/bookings.tsx`, parts of `viewer/workflows.tsx`) invoke it without `immediateDelete`, so the SendGrid send remains active. Cancellation is deferred to `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which only cancels `cancelled: true` reminders with `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. That creates a verifiable window where a cancelled/rescheduled booking can still have an active SendGrid scheduled send (e.g., if the cron isn’t running, or runs too late relative to the scheduled send), which is a behavior regression from the prior immediate cancellation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964 — The try/catch around forEach with un-awaited async delete calls can never catch anything, so the "Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders" log is dead code and failures pass silently.

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the new block wraps `workflowReminders.forEach(...)` in a `try/catch` but calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` without `await`. Any async rejection would not be caught by that `try/catch`, so the `log.error("Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders", error)` is effectively unable to report async failures. However, the diff also shows both delete functions are `async` but internally wrap their bodies in `try/catch` and only `console.log` on error (no rethrow), so this is more of misleading/ineffective error handling than a clearly verifiable functional defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — A single failed SendGrid cancel throws out of the whole loop, so later cancelled reminders never get cancelled and the deletes queued for earlier ones (lazy Prisma promises, never awaited) never run; the same batches get re-POSTed on every cron run until they age out.

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts the new cancellation block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop in a single `try/catch`. If any `await client.request(...)` throws, control jumps to `catch` and the function never reaches `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`, so any previously queued `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` promises are never awaited/executed. Additionally, because failed cancellations leave `WorkflowReminder` rows with `cancelled: true`, the same reminders will be re-selected by the next cron run and retried repeatedly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — The immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or flags the DB row, so on reschedule in handleNewBooking (no cascade) the row lingers as a live scheduled reminder and a failed cancel is swallowed with no retry.

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` the `immediateDelete` branch cancels the SendGrid batch and then `return`s without updating or deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row (`packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts`, immediateDelete block). Call sites in this diff pass `immediateDelete: true` (e.g. `handleNewBooking` reschedule cleanup and `workflows.tsx` on workflow/step deletion), and the previous explicit Prisma deletes were removed in those places. As a result, the DB row can remain with `referenceId`/`scheduled` unchanged and not marked `cancelled`, so the new cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders` (which only targets `cancelled: true`) will not pick it up, and any cancellation failure is swallowed by the catch with no retry mechanism shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:48 — Soft-cancelled reminders are only cancelled on a later cron run, so a reminder due before the next run (or under SendGrid's 10-minute cutoff) is still sent for a cancelled booking, and the past-due deleteMany then purges it with no cancel ever sent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes cancellation behavior so booking cancellation/reschedule often no longer immediately cancels the provider-side scheduled email. In handleCancelBooking.ts and viewer/bookings.tsx, reminders now call deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId) without `immediateDelete`, and emailReminderManager.ts in that case only sets `WorkflowReminder.cancelled = true` (it does not send the SendGrid cancel request). The actual SendGrid cancel + DB delete happens later in scheduleEmailReminders.ts by querying `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now+1h`. Until that cron/API job runs, the SendGrid scheduled send can still fire, so a reminder could be sent for a cancelled booking if it becomes due before the next run/cancellation window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:180 — If twilio.cancelSMS throws (for example, the SMS was already sent or cancelled), the workflowReminder row delete is skipped, leaving stale rows that the old code always deleted.

adjudication.rationale: In smsReminderManager.ts, deleteScheduledSMSReminder now performs `await twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and then deletes the Prisma row in the same `try` block. If `twilio.cancelSMS` throws, execution jumps to `catch` and the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId }})` is skipped, leaving the reminder row undeleted. In the old flow, callers separately queued `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id }})` regardless of Twilio cancellation outcome (and the Twilio cancel call wasn’t awaited), so the DB row would still be deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:968 — After requestReschedule has already soft-cancelled a booking's reminders, rebooking through handleNewBooking cancels the same batches immediately but leaves cancelled:true, so the cron POSTs a second cancel for an already-cancelled batch (which can hit the abort-on-error path).

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts (new block around ~950+), reschedule flow cancels reminders by calling deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true). In emailReminderManager.ts, when immediateDelete is true it POSTs a cancel to /v3/user/scheduled_sends and then returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or clearing/updating its cancelled flag. Separately, scheduleEmailReminders.ts now finds reminders with cancelled: true and scheduledDate within the next hour and POSTs another cancel for the same batch_id before deleting the row. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole loop and the lazily-built PrismaPromise deletes are never executed, so already-cancelled rows stay `cancelled: true` and get re-cancelled next run while later reminders go uncancelled

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` the new cancellation block wraps the entire loop in a single `try`/`catch`. Inside the `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop it `await`s the SendGrid cancel request, then only *builds* (does not `await`) a `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` promise and pushes it into `workflowRemindersToDelete`. If any `client.request(...)` throws for one reminder, execution jumps to `catch` before `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`, so none of the accumulated Prisma delete promises are executed (Prisma queries are lazy until awaited). This leaves `cancelled: true` rows in the DB to be reprocessed next run, and also stops processing later reminders in the list.

Since the DB row remains `cancelled: true`, the cron/API `scheduleEmailReminders` will later re-cancel those same reminders again (`findMany({ cancelled: true, scheduledDate <= +1h })` then POST cancel by `batch_id`). There is no guard against already-cancelled reminders, and the cron cancellation loop can abort on a single SendGrid error (await in `for...of` inside one try/catch), leaving remaining reminders undeleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20230217230604_add_cancelled_to_workflow_reminder/migration.sql:2 — No rollback plan: if app code is rolled back, rows already flagged `cancelled: true` are ignored by the old code and their SendGrid batches are never cancelled

Actual SendGrid cancellation for these soft-cancelled rows is deferred to `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which scans `WorkflowReminder` rows with `cancelled: true` and cancels them only when `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`, then deletes the row. If app code is rolled back after deploying this change (while keeping the migrated DB), the older codebase would not include this new deferred-cancellation sweep, so any reminders already only marked `cancelled: true` could indeed fail to get their SendGrid batches cancelled. This is an operational/rollback risk grounded in the new behavior, not a directly provable runtime bug in the new code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:180 — The DB delete now runs after twilio.cancelSMS in the same try block, so a Twilio error (e.g. message already sent or not cancelable) skips the row delete and leaks the WorkflowReminder row; the old code deleted rows independently of the Twilio call

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:523 — Un-awaited SMS and null-referenceId email helpers race the awaited workflowStep.delete cascade at line 527, so their prisma.workflowReminder.delete throws P2025 on already-cascaded rows, producing spurious error logs that hide real cancellation failures

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` the new cancellation calls are made inside `forEach` without `await` (e.g. for deleted steps: `remindersFromStep.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); })`). The helpers are `async` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` always performs `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)`, while `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` deletes when `referenceId` is null. Since `WorkflowReminder` has `onDelete: Cascade` from `WorkflowStep` (schema diff), an awaited `workflowStep.delete` later in the same codepath can cascade-delete the rows first, causing these un-awaited deletes to throw P2025 and be logged from the helper catch blocks, i.e., a real race/noisy-error condition introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — A single failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole loop and skips the lazy deletes, so the same row can fail again on every run and block all later soft-cancelled reminders, which then still email attendees about cancelled or rescheduled bookings (details and meeting URL)

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` the new “cancel reminders” logic wraps the entire cancellation loop in a single `try { ... for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...); workflowRemindersToDelete.push(prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)); } await Promise.all(...) } catch { ... }`. If any one `client.request` throws (e.g., SendGrid cancel fails for one `referenceId`), control jumps to the `catch` and the loop stops, so remaining cancelled reminders are not cancelled and their DB rows are not deleted. Those rows will be picked up again on the next run (still `cancelled: true`), potentially preventing later reminders from being processed and allowing scheduled emails for cancelled/rescheduled bookings to still go out.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — Untested cron cancel loop: a single SendGrid failure (e.g. batch already cancelled via the immediateDelete path) aborts the whole loop and the lazily-built prisma deletes never execute, so the same reminder blocks all later cancellations on every run

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop in a single `try`. Each iteration does `await client.request(...)` before enqueueing `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)`, and the deletes are only executed after the loop via `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. If any single SendGrid `client.request` throws, control jumps to `catch` and *none* of the queued Prisma deletes run (and later reminders in the loop are skipped), so the same `cancelled: true` reminders can repeatedly block progress on subsequent cron runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:203 — No tests cover the three new deleteScheduledEmailReminder branches (null referenceId hard-delete, immediateDelete SendGrid-only, soft-cancel update) even though every caller dropped the old `scheduled && referenceId` guard

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new branching behavior in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)`: hard-delete when `referenceId` is null, SendGrid cancel when `immediateDelete` is true, and soft-cancel via `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ cancelled: true })` otherwise. Multiple callers were changed to invoke it without the old `reminder.scheduled && reminder.referenceId` guard (e.g., `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `viewer/bookings.tsx`, `viewer/workflows.tsx`), so all three branches are now realistically exercised. The diff shows no new/updated tests accompanying this nontrivial behavioral change, but it does not show whether existing tests already cover these paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — immediateDelete branch cancels at SendGrid but neither deletes nor flags the DB row, leaving stale scheduled rows (e.g. after handleNewBooking reschedule) that can later be soft-cancelled and re-cancelled by cron; no test pins the expected row state

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (emailReminderManager.ts), the `immediateDelete` branch cancels the SendGrid scheduled send and then `return`s without updating or deleting the corresponding `WorkflowReminder` row. Unlike the non-immediate path (which sets `cancelled: true`) and the `!referenceId` path (which deletes the row), this leaves the DB record in an inconsistent/stale state after callers like `handleNewBooking`/workflows deletion call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`. This behavior is directly shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — Soft-cancelled reminders are only cancelled at SendGrid when cron sees them within 1 hour of scheduledDate; no test covers the timing window (cancel shortly before send, cron cadence gaps) so emails for cancelled bookings may still go out

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a soft-cancel path for email reminders: most call sites now invoke `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete`, which in `emailReminderManager.ts` only sets `cancelled: true` in DB (no SendGrid cancel). Actual SendGrid cancellation is deferred to `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which only looks for `cancelled: true` reminders with `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour` and then cancels/deletes them. That creates a real, diff-grounded timing/cadence risk (cancellation close to send depends on the cron/API running in that window), but whether emails “may still go out” depends on the external cron frequency which is not shown in the diff; also the claim about missing tests is plausible because no tests are added here, but not strictly provable. So it’s a specific edge-case/coverage concern rather than a verifiable defect in isolation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966 — New reschedule reminder-cancel path is untested, including original bookings already CANCELLED by requestReschedule (soft-cancelled rows re-cancelled immediately) and a try/catch that cannot catch the un-awaited async helper failures

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:485 — Reminder cancellation became fire-and-forget (removed from the awaited Promise.all) and no test asserts reminders are soft-cancelled/deleted once the cancel handler resolves

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the prior reminder deletion Prisma promises were collected and awaited via Promise.all; this diff removes that (`remindersToDelete` and its inclusion in `prismaPromises`) and now calls the async `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` inside nested `forEach` without `await`. Since those functions are `async` (see emailReminderManager.ts and smsReminderManager.ts), the cancel handler can resolve before reminders are actually soft-cancelled/deleted, making reminder cancellation effectively fire-and-forget.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:488 — requestReschedule reminder cancellation switched to un-awaited soft-cancel/SMS-delete with no test verifying old-booking reminders end up cancelled

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`, the previous implementation collected Prisma promises and `await`ed `Promise.all(remindersToDelete)`. The new code iterates `bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` and calls the async `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` without `await` or aggregating promises. Since both reminder-manager functions are `async` (return promises) and perform side effects (DB update/delete and external cancel), these cancellations can be skipped/unfinished before the mutation continues/returns, changing behavior compared to the prior awaited deletion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:179 — deleteScheduledSMSReminder now owns row deletion but skips it when twilio.cancelSMS throws; no test covers null referenceId, Twilio failure, or already-deleted row

adjudication.rationale: In smsReminderManager.ts, deleteScheduledSMSReminder wraps both Twilio cancellation and prisma.workflowReminder.delete() in a single try/catch. If twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId) throws, control jumps to catch and the DB row deletion is skipped entirely, even though this function is now the only place doing row deletion after the diff removed the caller-side deleteMany loops. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:519 — Step-deleted (and workflow-delete at line 212) paths race un-awaited reminder deletes against cascade deletes from workflowStep.delete/workflow.deleteMany; no router test covers these paths

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, multiple paths now call async reminder-cancellation helpers inside `forEach` without `await` (e.g., workflow delete path around line ~208: `scheduledReminders.forEach(... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true) / deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...) )`, and step-deleted path around ~529 does the same). Since the diff also removed the previously awaited Prisma `deleteMany` batches, these async operations are no longer waited on at all. In a serverless/short-lived request context this can cause cancellations/DB updates/deletes inside `deleteScheduled*Reminder` to be interrupted or race with subsequent workflow/workflowStep deletions (cascade), leading to reminders not being reliably cancelled/cleaned up. The "no router test covers these paths" portion is not verifiable from the diff, but the un-awaited async cancellation is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:376 — activeOn-removal and step-edit (line 574) paths changed from hard delete to soft-cancel for email reminders with no test asserting cancelled-flag vs deletion per reminder state

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the activeOn-removal path (`remindersToDelete.flat().forEach(...)` around the shown hunk near line ~373) and the step-edit path (`remindersToUpdate.forEach(...)` near line ~586) were changed from `ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany(...)` hard deletes to calling `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)`.

Per the diff in `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` no longer deletes by default when `referenceId` exists; it updates the DB record to `cancelled: true` (soft-cancel) unless `immediateDelete` is passed. That is a material behavior change that likely merits a targeted test asserting the intended outcome (deleted vs `cancelled=true`) depending on `referenceId`/immediateDelete. The diff does not show any such test addition.

(While there are also potential async/await concerns in these `forEach` usages, the finding is specifically about the soft-cancel vs delete behavior and lack of an asserting test.)
